title: Swim.com Workout Sync Gap Watch
dataSources: Swim.com workouts (`swimcom:workout`), MySwimPro sessions (`myswimpro:session`), pool lap logs (`pool:lap`), and swim meet results (`swim:meet`).
app: Swim.com workout exports, MySwimPro session logs, pool lap counters, swim meet results, and interval pace trackers forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=swimcom:workout
| stats max(_time) as last_seen by stroke_type
| eval hours_since=round((now()-last_seen)/3600,1)
| where hours_since>72
| sort - hours_since
description: Detects when Swim.com workout data has stopped arriving for a given stroke.
value: Personal telemetry is only useful when it is current; sync-gap alerts catch failed exports and broken credentials early.
implementation: Track the latest event time per stroke and alert when the feed is older than 72 hours.
visualization: Table of entities by hours since last event.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Swimming & Lap Training — typical feeds: Swim.com workouts (`swimcom:workout`), MySwimPro sessions (`myswimpro:session`), pool lap logs (`pool:lap`), and swim meet results (`swim:meet`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `swimcom:workout`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=swimcom:workout`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Swim.com workout exports, MySwimPro session logs, pool lap counters, swim meet results, and interval pace trackers forwarded to Splunk HEC..

**Author notes:** Track the latest event time per stroke and alert when the feed is older than 72 hours.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "swimcom:workout", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=swimcom:workout earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Swim.com Workout Sync Gap Watch** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=swimcom:workout`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `hours_since` (> 72) after max — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `hours_since`, `stroke_type`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=swimcom:workout
| stats max(_time) as last_seen by stroke_type
| eval hours_since=round((now()-last_seen)/3600,1)
| where hours_since>72
| sort - hours_since
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=swimcom:workout earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table hours_since, stroke_type
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=swimcom:workout earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `hours_since` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=swimcom:workout earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(hours_since) AS p50 perc90(hours_since) AS p90 perc99(hours_since) AS p99 max(hours_since) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.103.6: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Table Of Entities By Hours Since Last Event (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `swimcom:workout` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=swimcom:workout | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
